api:
<Horizon data={ticks} x={|t: &Tick| t.time} x_axis={AxisConfig::new().time()}>
    <TrendSeries name="CPU Δ" y={|t: &Tick| t.cpu} />
    <TrendSeries name="Latency Δ" y={|t: &Tick| t.latency} />
</Horizon>
PropTypeDefault
dataas aboverequired
xFn(&T) -> f64required
children<TrendSeries>: one horizon row each; name is the row labelrequired
bandsusize: shades per sign3
positive, negativecoloursgood and bad
x_axisAxisConfigAxisConfig::new()
classTailwind classes ("h-64")

Each row is cut into bands equal slices of its largest absolute value. The slices are stacked on top of each other, darker for bigger values, and negative values are flipped up in the negative colour. A row takes a fraction of the height a normal line chart would need. The slice size is shown next to each row's name.

examples.title: Three metrics
examples.description: Each row folds its values into 3 bands; darker means further from zero, red is below zero.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn servers() {
    let data = use_signal(ticks());
    rsx! {
        <Horizon data={data} x={|t: &Tick| t.time} x_axis={AxisConfig::new().time()} class="h-56">
            <TrendSeries name="CPU Δ" y={|t: &Tick| t.cpu} />
            <TrendSeries name="Memory Δ" y={|t: &Tick| t.memory} />
            <TrendSeries name="Latency Δ" y={|t: &Tick| t.latency} />
        </Horizon>
    }
}
